source_of_truth: Read by hand from the Nuxt project: pages/billing.vue names middleware: 'subscription-guard' in definePageMeta, but middleware/ holds only analytics.global.ts and staff.ts; no file, layer or addRouteMiddleware registers 'subscription-guard' and no auth module is installed, so this is a confirmed unknown-middleware (Nuxt throws at runtime). analytics.global.ts is not auth-like by name and its body only logs (no user/session/navigateTo), so it is not a global auth guard. pages/reports.vue carries no middleware, is not a public/auth route, and there is no global auth middleware, so it is an unguarded private-looking page. pages/login.vue is a public route by the default regex and must not be flagged.
provenance: blind generalization: truth derived from source without consulting tool output

expected.rationale: billing.vue references 'subscription-guard', which exists in no middleware file, no Nuxt layer and no addRouteMiddleware call, and no auth module could register it; the project-level finding carries no file/line.
/reports has no page middleware, is not a public/auth route, and there is no global auth middleware; it is an unguarded private-looking page (heuristic, no line).

forbidden.why_not_a_defect: billing.vue declares middleware in definePageMeta, so it is guarded even though the named middleware is missing (that is the unknown-middleware finding, not a missing-guard finding).
/login matches the default public-route regex, so it is intentionally public and must not be flagged as unguarded.
